text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High rate of TLS handshake failures for service=redwood-inference-api region=eu-west-1. p50 latency stable, 5xx_rate=18% over 10m, affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Pager: @alex. Incident ID: INC-2026-889. Alert group: tls_handshake_failures. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/INC-2026-889

alex: seeing it. I'm the oncall. ACK.

alex: quick note — who owns cert-rotation runbooks? could be certs or network.

carla: cert rotation party last night for internal CA, but rotation job reported success. tagging logs.

maya: I'm waking up, will join in 2 minutes. Any customer reports?

support-bot: Escalation: 4 active customer incidents (EU customers), highest severity P1. Affected: inference-hosted, embeddings.

alex: ok triage plan: 1) collect TLS handshake failure logs from LB and inference nodes 2) check recent cert rotations and KMS events 3) verify VPC peering and MTU 4) mitigation: roll back cert if needed or enable failover pool.

jon: grabbing load balancer TLS logs now. seeing TLS alert types: "tls: handshake failure" and "alert handshake_failure" from multiple client IP prefixes.

alex: paste of LB error sample:
```
2026-03-15T02:10:04Z lb-1 eu-west tls: handshake failure: remote error: tls: bad certificate
client_ip=52.16.12.9 route=/v1/generate
```

carla: cert rotation job log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T01:58:22Z cert-rotator: rotated cert inference-api-eu-2026-03-15.pem -> inference-api-eu-2026-03-15-rot.pem
2026-03-15T01:58:23Z cert-rotator: reload nginx successful (exit=0)
```

alex: that's suspicious — rotator shows success but handshakes started ~12m after rotate. timeframe:
- 01:58 rotate job
- 02:05 first TLS errors appear (small)
- 02:10 errors spike (alert fired)

maya: hypothesis H1: new cert missing intermediate chain or wrong SANs. H2: certain clients fail due to MTU/fragmentation making cert exchange fail. H3: routing to wrong backend (old cert) due to VPC peering flaps.

jon: I pulled nginx config on a few nodes, cert path points to the new file. fingerprint matches the new cert.

carla: checking CA chain on the new cert...

carla: found: intermediate not included in the bundle on storage for one zone. Looks like rotator didn't concat intermediate for eu-west-1b.

alex: good find. if missing intermediate, some clients (older TLS stacks) might reject. But why handshake_failure and also 5xx? Some clients should still succeed.

david: I'm seeing some SYN retransmits and large packet drops on the peering interface between eu-west vpc-a and vpc-services. counters: dropped pkts ~5000 in 10m, errors on enP3s0 at 02:08. MTU mismatch between CNI and peer?

maya: can you paste netstat/snmp?

jon: netstat ifconfig from a node:
```
eth0 mtu 1500
peer0 mtu 1400
```

alex: aha — MTU 1500 vs peer 1400. That can cause TLS handshake fragmentation issues, especially with larger certificate chains. Hypothesis H4: missing intermediate + MTU mismatch => handshake fails during certificate transfer.

sre_lead: prioritize immediate mitigations: 1) re-deploy cert bundle including intermediate to all zones; 2) temporarily adjust MTU on peer or enable TCP MSS clamping on load balancers; 3) add fallback routing to legacy ingress that uses older cert chain. Which is fastest?

alex: fastest: push corrected cert bundle to nginx and reload, and open a change to enable MSS clamping on LB (config change). I'll coordinate cert push.

carla: rolling a fix: uploading new bundle with full chain to artifact store and triggering rotator dry-run.

carla: pushed to eu-west-1a,b,c and triggered nginx reload via orchestrator: all nodes reported OK.

jon: enabling MSS clamping on ALB -> config snippet:
```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:... --protocol TCP --default-actions ... --set-tcp-mss=1360
```
applied to edge-alb-eu-west-1 in prod.

alex: monitoring metrics. dashboard shows error rate dropping from 18% -> 3% over 7 minutes. p50 latency stable.

support-bot: Customer Impact update: 4 customers moved to degraded -> recovered state. No new P1s created. Notifying accounts.

maya: great. timeline draft for RCA:
- 01:58 cert-rotator rotated cert but omitted intermediate in one zone (eu-west-1b) due to a packaging bug.
- 02:05 initial handshake failures observed.
- 02:08 concurrent peering MTU mismatch caused fragmentation, amplifying failures for many clients.
- 02:10 alert fired.
- 02:15 fix: pushed full cert chain to all zones and reloaded nginx.
- 02:20 mitigation: enabled MSS clamping on ALB.
- 02:30 error rate back to baseline.

alex: will document hypotheses and evidence in the post-incident RCA. For the in-incident thread, I'm tagging evidence: logs.tar.gz link: https://artifacts.redwood/logs/INC-2026-889/logs.tar.gz

jon: adding packet captures here: https://artifacts.redwood/pcaps/INC-2026-889/pcap-02-08.pcap (shows fragmented cert exchange)

carla: rotator job code snippet that caused missing intermediate:
```
# rotator stack: builds cert bundle by concatenating cert and intermediate from S3 keys
interp_key = s3.get(last_success_key + "-intermediate")
if not interp_key: # bug: empty string check failed, skipped concat
    log.warn("missing intermediate for {}", zone)
```

alex: next actions:
- short-term: ship a patch to rotator to validate bundle completeness and add preflight checks (sha256 of bundle).
- medium-term: add synthetic tests across MTU sizes and client stacks during cert rollouts.
- long-term: make rotator perform zero-downtime dual-stack serving (serve both old and new chain for 5m).

sre_lead: also open infra ticket to normalize MTU across peering interfaces and add MTU alerts.

maya: handing off to oncall-next @jon for post-incident writeup and follow-ups. Jon, you good to take it?

jon: taking post-incident. I'll build a timeline + actions + owners. I'll kick off a postmortem doc and link here.

alex: thanks team. final status: incident RESOLVED at 02:30 UTC. root cause: cert-rotator packaging bug causing missing intermediate + MTU mismatch between VPC peering path that increased likelihood of handshake failures.

jon: postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood/pm/INC-2026-889 (draft). Assigning action owners: CARLA -> rotator fix, INFRA -> MTU normalization, SRE -> add MSS clamping runbook.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers with summary and mitigation steps.

carla: notes for RCA: include code diff, test coverage, and safety rollouts.

alex: good work. I'll update runbook with explicit cert bundle verification step and add a preflight smoke that validates handshake from multiple client fingerprints. :thumbsup:

jon: closing thread after PM draft posted.
